findings.title: Paid booking cancellation returns before cancelling scheduled reminders/jobs
findings.body: The handler refunds paid bookings and returns before reaching the scheduled-job cancellation and workflow reminder cancellation code later in the function. As a result, cancelled/rejected paid bookings can keep active workflow reminders and scheduled jobs, so reminder emails/SMS may still be sent.

findings.title: Workflow reminder cancellations are fired without being awaited
findings.body: The cancellation loop calls async deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder inside forEach but never collects or awaits the promises. The request can finish before SendGrid/Twilio cancellation and Prisma writes complete, especially in serverless environments, leaving reminders active or inconsistently cancelled.

findings.title: Paid branch awaits an array instead of its promises
findings.body: `await apiDeletes` awaits the array object, not `Promise.all(apiDeletes)`. Calendar/video deletion promises in the paid cancellation path are therefore not waited for, can reject as unhandled rejections, and external events may remain while the API reports success.

findings.title: Reschedule path cancels old reminders without awaiting promises
findings.body: originalRescheduledBooking.workflowReminders.forEach invokes async deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder without awaiting them. The surrounding try/catch cannot catch asynchronous rejections, so the reschedule can complete before the old reminders are actually cancelled.

findings.title: Reschedule uses immediate SendGrid cancellation without persisting cancellation state
findings.body: deleteScheduledEmailReminder is called with immediateDelete=true for rescheduled bookings. That path only calls SendGrid and does not delete or mark the WorkflowReminder row. If the SendGrid call fails or is not awaited, there is no local cancelled state and no retry, so the old reminder can still be sent.

findings.title: Deferred cancellation can miss reminders that occur before the next cron run
findings.body: The non-immediate cancellation path only sets cancelled=true and relies on a cron job that runs every 15 minutes. If a booking is cancelled shortly before a reminder's scheduled time and the next cron run happens after that time, SendGrid can send the reminder before cancellation is applied.

findings.title: Cancelled-reminder query does not restrict to scheduled email reminders with a batch ID
findings.body: remindersToCancel finds all rows with cancelled=true and scheduledDate within an hour, without filtering method: EMAIL, scheduled: true, or referenceId not null. A cancelled SMS row or an email row without a SendGrid batch ID can cause invalid SendGrid requests and block processing of valid cancellations.

findings.title: One failing SendGrid cancellation stops processing of all remaining cancellations
findings.body: The try/catch surrounds the entire cancellation loop. If client.request throws for any reminder, the remaining cancelled reminders are neither cancelled nor deleted. A single bad or transient record can repeatedly prevent the cron job from cancelling any cancelled emails.

findings.title: Unscheduled email reminders are scheduled without checking cancelled flag or booking status
findings.body: The unscheduledReminders query filters only by method EMAIL, scheduled false, and scheduledDate. It does not exclude cancelled=true rows or verify that the associated booking is still accepted. Stale reminders for cancelled or rescheduled bookings can therefore be scheduled and emailed.

findings.title: immediateDelete cancels SendGrid but does not update/delete the local reminder
findings.body: When immediateDelete is true and referenceId exists, deleteScheduledEmailReminder sends a cancellation to SendGrid and returns without deleting the WorkflowReminder or setting cancelled. Unless the caller separately deletes the row after success, failed cancellations are not retried and local state no longer reflects the scheduled email.

findings.title: Reschedule mutation cancels workflow reminders without awaiting them
findings.body: bookingToReschedule.workflowReminders.forEach calls async deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder but does not await the promises. The mutation can return before reminders are marked cancelled/deleted, so a cancelled/rescheduled booking may still have active reminders.

findings.title: Workflow deletion cancels reminders asynchronously and then deletes the workflow
findings.body: scheduledReminders.forEach starts SendGrid/Twilio cancellations without awaiting them, then the workflow is deleted. Cascade deletion can remove the local reminder records before provider cancellation completes; if cancellation fails or is interrupted, scheduled emails/SMS remain active and cannot be retried.

findings.title: Cancellations for disabled event types are not awaited
findings.body: In the workflow update mutation, remindersToDelete.flat().forEach calls async deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder without awaiting them before deleting relationships and scheduling new reminders. Reminders for event types that are no longer active may remain active if the async work fails or terminates early.

findings.title: Workflow update does not await processing of existing steps
findings.body: userWorkflow.steps.map(async ...) creates promises for deleting/updating steps, cancelling old reminders, and scheduling replacements, but the promises are never awaited. The mutation can return before cancellations and scheduling finish, leaving old reminders active or new reminders missing.

findings.title: No tests for new cancelled reminder cron/cancellation behavior
findings.body: The PR introduces a new cancelled flag and cron-based cancellation logic but adds no automated tests verifying that cancelled/rescheduled bookings do not receive reminders, that the cron cancels only due cancelled emails, and that a failing cancellation does not block the queue.
